items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Topics 6:1
items.html: The original ten Sefirot from the aspect of the Malchut of restriction 2, which begin from AA, as above in answer 25, are called the nine original Sefirot. And they are only three Sefirot: Bina, ZA, and Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Topics 6:2
items.html: Because this Malchut is the bottom Hey that rose to the Einayim, and split the ten Sefirot of Keter into two Partzufim, for Atik took Keter and Hochma, and Bina and ZON went out outside of Atik and became the nine Sefirot of AA, namely through the correction of the lines, for the three lines of Bina are called HBD, and the three lines of ZA are called HGT, and the three lines of the Nukva are called NHY. And it is found that three vessels — Bina, ZA, and Nukva — became the nine Sefirot. And from here is the root that there are no more than three vessels in any Partzuf: Bina, ZA, and Malchut. For since in AA there are only these three vessels, which is the Keter and root of all of Atzilut, therefore there are no more than these three in all the Partzufim below it, which are its branches. Thus Keter and Hochma of the original ten Sefirot are in Atik, and Bina and ZON are in AA. (Vol. 1, p. 304, Item 18).
